title: Lock out a travel adapter's UK pins with its side toggle, then push the adapter fully into a UK socket
instruction: Push the middle toggle on the side of the travel adapter all the way down until the UK pins click out and lock, then plug the adapter into the extension lead's socket, push it in until it sits flat on the socket, and let go.
context: Anyone travelling to the UK, Ireland or Singapore does this in a hotel room: a universal travel adapter keeps its pin sets inside, and you push the toggle for the country's pins along its slot until they click out and lock, then push the adapter into the socket. The toggle needs about 3 N and must go its whole 22.8 mm: the catch only drops in at the very end. Stop short and the pins are not locked, and the socket's sprung contacts (about 8 N to push home) push them back into the adapter. The small toggle sits between two others 11 mm away, so one hand holds the adapter while the other pushes just that toggle. The three pins must then enter openings only 0.75 mm wider than they are, so the adapter has to come down square and centred, and be pushed until its base sits flat on the socket.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. 1) Socket: a Masterplug EXS1315B-01 single-socket heavy-duty extension lead (black, 90 x 60 x 33, BS 1363 socket, safety shuttered), lying flat with its socket face up, its long side along y, centred at (280, -115), the socket's earth opening toward the robot, its cable running off along -y; held to the table with double-sided tape. Its plug is never put into the mains: nothing is live. 2) Adapter: an EPICKA TA-105 universal travel adapter (71.1 x 50.0 x 52.1, 190 g, grey), all pin sets in, standing on its pin face with its long side along y, its pin face centred at (200, -140), its three toggles (US/AU, UK, EU from -y to +y) on the side facing the robot. The UK toggle is the middle one. Pin sizes are BS 1363: line and neutral 6.4 x 4.0, 17.7 long, 22.2 apart; earth 4.0 x 8.0, 22.3 long. Start: both arms at their ready pose, grippers open. Estimates (no published figure; one-minute checks in the README): toggle force ~3 N and travel 22.8, toggle size and spacing, pin positions on the adapter, opening clearance 0.75 per side, push to plug in ~8 N (check: extension lead on a kitchen scale, read the peak while pushing the adapter in), frictions.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run from the trial video, a photo and a ruler. Locked out: the UK toggle sits at the end of its slot and the UK pins stand fully out (earth pin 22.3, the others 17.7 from the adapter's base); pressing the pins with a finger does not move them. In the socket: all three pins are inside their openings. Gap: how far the adapter's base stands above the socket face at its highest corner (ruler or feeler card). Released: the centre point between each gripper's fingers (about 13 mm back from the fingertips) at least 3 cm from the adapter, and the adapter has been still for 1 s. Score 0 if the pins are not locked out, the adapter is not released or still moving, or it fell off the table (doing nothing scores 0). Otherwise: 1.0 if in the socket with a gap of 1.5 mm or less (flush); 0.75 if in the socket with a gap over 1.5 and up to 6 mm; 0.5 if in the socket with a gap over 6 mm; 0.25 if the pins are locked out but not in the socket's openings.
reset_notes: About 30 seconds, nothing is used up. Pull the adapter straight out of the socket. Press and hold its lock button and slide the UK toggle back up to the top of its slot so all the pins are inside, then let go of the button. Stand the adapter on its pin face at its start mark (a pencil outline on the table, 71 x 50 mm, centred at (200, -140)), toggles facing the robot. Check the extension lead is still taped down at its mark, socket face up and unplugged from the mains. Return both arms to the ready pose.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, no electricity. The pin carrier is a slide with 2 N of stiction; the lock is a sprung catch that drops over a rail on the carrier in the last 0.8 mm (inner layout estimated; the release button is not modelled). The socket's line and neutral contacts are sprung plates (~8 N to push home, estimate); its shutters are not modelled. Opening clearance 0.75 mm with 1 mm lead-ins, toggle and pin positions are estimates from the maker's drawings.
